slides.title: High-Level Concurrency with concurrent.futures
slides.prompt: The `concurrent.futures` module offers a unified high-level interface for asynchronous execution using worker pools (`ThreadPoolExecutor` for I/O tasks and `ProcessPoolExecutor` for CPU tasks).
slides.codeSnippet:
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

def fetch(url):
    return f"Data from {url}"

urls = ["url1", "url2", "url3"]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as executor:
    results = list(executor.map(fetch, urls))
print(results)

slides.title: Executor Map Method Behavior
options: It applies the function across an iterable concurrently and yields results in the original order
It runs functions sequentially without thread pooling
It returns futures in order of completion rather than input order
It requires a custom callback function
slides.correctAnswer: It applies the function across an iterable concurrently and yields results in the original order

slides.title: Context Manager Exit Behavior for Executors
slides.prompt: What occurs automatically when exiting a `with ThreadPoolExecutor()` context block?
options: It implicitly invokes `executor.shutdown(wait=True)`, waiting for pending futures to finish
It instantly cancels all running and pending threads
It raises a RuntimeError if futures remain unfinished
It detaches threads into background OS daemons
slides.correctAnswer: It implicitly invokes `executor.shutdown(wait=True)`, waiting for pending futures to finish
